post.summary: Sign in with email and password (plus the two-step code when on; email-code users get a code sent and 401 twofa_required). An expired temporary password is 400 temp_password_expired

code.description: 6-digit code when the account has two-step sign-in; a missing code gives 401 twofa_required with method (app|email) and, for email, sent_to (masked address) and resend_after (seconds). The email code is sent by that same call. Email channel off or unconfigured: 503 twofa_email_unavailable, never password-only

post.summary: Send a new two-step email code during sign-in (needs the password again; 429 resend_too_soon within 60 s, too_many_codes after 5 per hour)

resend_after.description: Seconds before another code can be sent (60)

post.summary: Sign out

Finish an SSO sign-in: the page posts the code and state from /sso/callback with its binding; the box exchanges the code, checks the ID token and signs the person in like a password sign-in (session and CSRF cookies). 400 sso_expired, 400 sso_failed, 403 no_access, 403 email_unverified, 403 disabled, 409 email_in_use, 502 idp_unreachable

Start an SSO sign-in: returns the identity provider address to open, with state, nonce and a PKCE challenge, and a binding the page keeps until the callback. 400 oidc_off when SSO is off or not set up, 502 idp_unreachable when the discovery document cannot be read, 429 rate_limited

authorize_url.description: The identity provider's authorization endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state, nonce, code_challenge (S256)

binding.description: Random value the page keeps in session storage and sends back with the callback, so the sign-in can only finish in the tab that started it

anyOf.description: app = authenticator app (TOTP), email = 6-digit code sent to the sign-in email

sso.description: The account signs in only through SSO: no Vedette password, two-step sign-in is the identity provider's

available.description: true only when the notify module is on and an email channel is configured and enabled

reason.description: Why the email method cannot be chosen, null when available

sent_to.description: Masked sign-in email where codes would go

post.summary: Authenticator app: confirm the TOTP key with a 6-digit code to turn on two-step sign-in
Turn off two-step sign-in (needs the password)
Email code: enter the code to prove the mailbox works and turn on two-step sign-in (expires in 10 min, single use, 5 wrong tries cancel it)
Email code: send a 6-digit code to my own sign-in email (409 when the email channel is not ready or two-step is already on; same limits as sign-in codes; needs the current password)

resend_after.description: Seconds before another code can be sent (60)

post.summary: Authenticator app: create a TOTP key waiting for confirmation (needs the current password; wrong password 400 wrong_password, counted like a failed sign-in)

secret.description: 20-byte base32 key (RFC 4648), typed by hand into the authenticator app

post.summary: Change password (needs the current password). The same call ends the temporary-password limit: the new password must differ from the temporary one

Connections to devices and services that response actions and the AI use: HTTP API, SSH, RESTCONF, automation platform, MCP server

target.description: Base URL or host:port. "mcp-stdio" rows are not supported

header.description: Token sign-in only: the name of the header the token is sent in, for a device whose API wants a key header. null sends Authorization: Bearer <token>. The token itself stays in the vault

last4.description: Last 4 characters of a token or password; null for an SSH key and for no sign-in. The full secret is never returned (SYS-4)

key_fingerprint.description: SSH key only: SHA256:<base64> fingerprint of the saved private key, like GitHub shows for a key. The mock uses a hash of the key body; the backend computes the public-key fingerprint

username.description: User name for SSH and for Basic sign-in; null for the other sign-ins

kind.description: tls_sha256 = SHA-256 of the public key (SubjectPublicKeyInfo) of the HTTPS leaf certificate, when no public authority vouches for the chain; tls_roots = a public authority vouched for the chain at the first test, and every later test requires that again (a self-signed certificate is refused); ssh_hostkey = the SSH server host key

value.description: tls_sha256: 64 hex characters; tls_roots: "system roots"; ssh_hostkey: key type and SHA256 fingerprint

anyOf.description: Pinned at the first successful Test (trust on first use). A changed certificate or host key is refused until an administrator forgets the pin

pin.description: Read-only. null until the first Test, or after the pin was forgotten

allow.description: Hosts, URL prefixes or commands that may be used through this connection

kind.description: tls_sha256 = SHA-256 of the public key (SubjectPublicKeyInfo) of the HTTPS leaf certificate, when no public authority vouches for the chain; tls_roots = a public authority vouched for the chain at the first test, and every later test requires that again (a self-signed certificate is refused); ssh_hostkey = the SSH server host key

value.description: tls_sha256: 64 hex characters; tls_roots: "system roots"; ssh_hostkey: key type and SHA256 fingerprint

anyOf.description: Pinned at the first successful Test (trust on first use). A changed certificate or host key is refused until an administrator forgets the pin

pin.description: Read-only. null until the first Test, or after the pin was forgotten

allow.description: Hosts, URL prefixes or commands that may be used through this connection

get.summary: Download a backup (password hashes, never passwords or keys)
Backups the operating system helper keeps on this box; 409 not_appliance on a container-only install

kind.description: manual = Download backup or a backup by hand; pre_os_update / pre_update / pre_restore = taken by the box before an operating system install, a Vedette update or a restore

includes_key.description: Holds the decryption key, so it restores on this box without the key file

get.summary: Export my data as JSON (every table except secrets; 409 busy while another export runs)

post.summary: Download the decryption key once, to keep apart from the backups: without it a backup restores on another box with its saved secrets and two-step sign-in lost. The current password (400 wrong_password, counted like a failed sign-in, 429 rate_limited) and, when two-step sign-in is on, a fresh code (400 code_required / invalid_code), as for the purge; audited (data.key_download). The 32 bytes of vedette.key, never logged

Delete all data back to a fresh install and replace the decryption key. Needs the exact organization name (400 confirm_mismatch), the current password (400 wrong_password, counted like a failed sign-in, 429 rate_limited) and, when two-step sign-in is on, a fresh code (400 code_required / invalid_code). 409 busy while a host run, an update or another purge runs; 502 host_unreachable when the configured helper does not answer, its socket missing included (nothing is deleted); 412 transition_pending; 500 backups_already_deleted when the purge fails after the helper deleted its backups (the data on the box is still there). kept lists what was not done or not touched (host_backups: this box is configured without a helper, so there were no helper backups to delete; honeypot_log: the raw log of the honeypot belongs to its container and stays; key_not_replaced: the new key could not be written, replace vedette.key by hand)

Restore a backup kept on this box: core first takes a copy of the current data, kept as a pre_restore backup, and the helper puts it back by itself when the restored data does not start. 409 confirm_required without confirm_data_loss: true; 404 backup_unknown; then the current password (400 wrong_password, counted like a failed sign-in, 429 rate_limited) and, when two-step sign-in is on, a fresh code (400 code_required / invalid_code), as for the purge; 409 busy, low_disk, schema_newer, not_appliance; 412 secrets_missing; 502 checksum_mismatch

confirm_data_loss.description: Required (true): everything written since the backup is replaced

status.description: reverted = the restored data did not start, so the box put back the data from before the restore

pre_restore_backup_id.description: The copy of the data from before the restore, kept in the list as pre_restore

error.description: Only when not done: why, in words

post.summary: First-run setup: create the organization and administrator, choose a module bundle, or use sample data. A bundle leaves out the modules this install cannot run (available false); naming one under custom gives 409 not_appliance

sample.description: true = use sample data and sign in as the sample administrator; other fields are ignored

commitment.description: true = the user confirms the ranges belong to their company and they may scan them actively

setup_code.description: The one-time setup code the box prints in its log while setup is open. Required to create the first administrator: missing or wrong gives 403 invalid_setup_code, 429 rate_limited after repeated wrong tries

accept_terms.description: true = the administrator read, understood and agrees to the terms of use (TERMS.md). Required to create the first administrator: anything else gives 400 terms_not_accepted, judged right after the setup code

get.summary: Modules and dependencies for the bundle step (does not reveal what is on), and the install kind for the setup code hint and the modules this install cannot run

available.description: false: this install cannot run the module (needs_host in its manifest on a container-only install: honeypot, credentialed scans); turning it on answers 409 not_appliance

install.description: appliance: installed by install.sh, with the system helper vedette-host; container: container-only install on the customer's Docker or Podman, no helper. The one place the GUI learns it

lan.description: The network of the box's management address (CIDR, like 192.168.18.0/24), offered as the first range of the network step; null when setup is done, on a container-only install, or when the box has no private IPv4 address

get.summary: The first-run restore while setup is open: running, or how it ended (reverted, failed); null before one. Once setup is done it is done (a restore that succeeded brings an organization that finished setup), whoever finished setup: nothing more than GET /setup says

status.description: reverted = the restored data did not start, so the box put back the fresh install

error.description: Only when not done: why, in words

post.summary: First-run restore, step 2: restore the uploaded backup as the box's data, with the setup code. With key (the key file downloaded from Settings -> Data, base64) the saved secrets and two-step sign-in come back; a key that is not 32 bytes is 400 invalid_key, one that opens none of the backup's secrets 400 wrong_key, before anything changes. Without key, a backup that holds secrets needs confirm_without_key: true (409 confirm_required). 404 upload_unknown when the upload is gone (older than an hour); 409 already_setup, busy, low_disk, schema_newer, not_appliance as for a restore

key.description: The decryption key file, base64

confirm_without_key.description: Required (true) without key when the backup holds secrets: they are lost and two-step users cannot sign in

accept_terms.description: true = the operator read, understood and agrees to the terms of use; anything else gives 400 terms_not_accepted, judged right after the setup code

status.description: reverted = the restored data did not start, so the box put back the fresh install

error.description: Only when not done: why, in words

post.summary: First-run restore, step 1: upload a backup downloaded from Settings -> Data (the .tar.gz as the body). Only before setup is done (409 already_setup) and with the setup code (403 invalid_setup_code, 429 rate_limited like setup). The box checks the file (400 not_a_backup: not a Vedette backup, damaged, or of a box never set up; 409 schema_newer: made by a newer Vedette), keeps it for an hour and says what it holds and what the decryption key changes. 409 not_appliance on a container-only install, 409 busy while another upload is checked, 409 low_disk, 413 over 4 GiB

schema.description: The setup code from the box's log, as for POST /core/setup

id.description: The uploaded backup, kept on the box for an hour; POST /core/setup/restore names it

created_at.description: When the backup was made (its manifest)

twofa_users.description: Active accounts that sign in with two-step: without the decryption key they cannot sign in

admins_without_key.description: Active administrators who can still sign in when the restore has no decryption key (password sign-in, no two-step); 0 = nobody could run the box without the key

secrets.description: Saved secrets (AI and feed keys, channel passwords, tokens, two-step keys): without the key they must be entered again

get.summary: The terms of use this box ships and who accepted them, when and which version; the text is TERMS.md, which the interface carries

version.description: The version of TERMS.md this box ships: its Version date and the first 8 hex digits of its SHA-256, like 2026-11-14.3f2a9c1b

by.description: The email of the administrator setup created, or "setup" for the operator who restored the box from a backup with the setup code; null unless the caller is an administrator (viewers and operators cannot list users)

version.description: The version accepted

via.description: setup = in the first-run setup; restore = before the first-run restore from a backup

accepted.description: null on a box set up before the terms step existed, or restored from such a backup and not yet settled

Alerts that name this CVE

Rows to skip, default 0

dst_ip.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address as the event names it

dst_port.description: null when the event gives no port (ICMP)

proto.description: Transport as the event wrote it, lower case: tcp, udp, icmp; empty when it gives none

dst_device.description: The inventory device with the destination address: the device that was attacked; null when none has it

cves.description: The CVE ids the event names, sorted; empty when it names none

findings.description: Findings of dst_device for the CVEs in cves; empty when the device is not affected or not in the inventory

incidents.description: Incidents of this kind with activity in the window

total.description: Bad-address hits seen through the mirror port in the window

delete.summary: Restore an IP from the Ignored list: detection may add it again the next time the box sees it. It is not added by this call and is not scannable by itself (it still needs ownership proof and the commitment). 404 when the IP is not on the list

put.summary: Turn auto-detect on or off and set the check interval (5 to 1440 minutes, else 400 bad_interval). Turning it on checks at once. The IP list is kept when it is turned off. Typing an IP is not possible here either

auto.description: On: the box detects its public IPs at first start and then every interval_min minutes. Off: only "Detect now". Default on

interval_min.description: Minutes between automatic checks, 5 to 1440. Default 60

message.description: What the last check saw, or why it failed

last_run.description: The last automatic or manual detection; null before the first one

retry_in_min.description: null while attempts are left. When the 10 attempts an hour (shared by Detect now and the Verify again of an IP; the DNS Check of a domain has its own limit of one per 30 seconds per target) are used up: minutes until the next one is possible, 1 or more

post.summary: "Detect now": the box asks three public "what is my IP" services (checkip.amazonaws.com, icanhazip.com, ifconfig.me/ip) over several rounds of new connections, accepts an IP only when at least two of the three agree in a round, and adds or renews (30 days from now) every IP that passed, except those on the Ignored list, so several egress IPs behind a load balancer are all found. Takes no IP input; refuses private, reserved and CGNAT results (400 not_public when none is public); 502 unreachable when no round gave an IP (no service answered, or they did not agree); rate limited to 10 attempts per hour

status.description: expired only exists for IPs: the box has not seen this IP for more than 30 days

token.description: Domain: the token in the TXT record vedette-verify=<token> (not secret, it is public in DNS). Typed IP: the token the proof file carries (ip_proof). IP the box found: empty string

verified_at.description: Domain: first successful verification. IP the box found: the last time the box saw this IP (every sighting renews it). Typed IP: the last time its proof was found

expires_at.description: IP: verified_at + 30 days (the proof expiry of a typed IP). Domain: null (the TXT record is re-checked right before every scan)

validity.description: IPs only: expiring = 5 days or less left

version.description: Version of the sentence the administrator saw next to Scan now; null on a commitment recorded by an older version

sentence.description: The exact sentence, with the target in it, kept with who and when; null on a commitment recorded by an older version

commitment.description: Recorded by the first Scan now of an administrator with two-step sign-in: who, when and the exact sentence shown next to the button

commitment_notice.description: The sentence the first Scan now of an administrator confirms, with this target in it; null once the target has a commitment of the current sentence; an older one is asked again once, so a target with a commitment can carry it too

text.description: The exact terms the administrator accepted, with the tick's sentence as the last line when ticked

disruptive.description: The extra tick: denial of service, password guessing, default-password sign-ins and exploit checks that send more than a harmless read too

terms.description: the acceptance of the testing terms; null when none. An acceptance of an older version does not count (full_scan is false) until accepted again

text.description: The terms with the target in them, one paragraph per line

disruptive.description: The sentence of the extra tick, off by default

terms_notice.description: The current testing terms for this target, to accept or to read again

terms_warning.description: GET of one IP target only: the box reaches the Internet through carrier-grade NAT (its gateway is in 100.64.0.0/10), so the address is probably shared; the disruptive tick is refused (409 shared_address) while it shows

full_scan.description: Scans of this target are deep scans: the current testing terms are accepted. Otherwise the scope of the Scan now sentence

blocked_reason.description: Why it cannot be scanned yet; null = can be scanned. ip_not_current (IPs only): the last full check that got an answer did not see the IP and no check since has, so scans are paused (until a later check sees it) while the IP stays in the list; verified_at is when the box last saw it

last_scan_at.description: When the newest scan started: every page names a scan by its start

last_scan_finished_at.description: When the newest scan ended (its OpenVAS step is its last); null while OpenVAS still runs, when never scanned, or when not known

last_seen.description: Set only on a port the newest scan did not report, kept from an earlier scan: the day a scan last saw it open (INV-22)

misses.description: With last_seen: how many scans in a row that checked the address missed the port (1 = missed by the last scan)

unchecked.description: The newest scan did not check the address: the row is as an earlier scan left it

ident.description: How service identification named the service: probed (a probe's answer, or the surface scan's GET read a product), port (only the usual service of the port number: not confirmed), none (nothing identified: service is unknown, ssl/unknown or tcpwrapped). Missing: identification did not run on the port, or an older scan

server.description: The HTTP Server header on the port (deep scan, http-server-header)

location.description: Where the port's first page redirects, when the deep scan did not follow it (http-title)

alt_host.description: The alternative Name: "_vedette-verify" or "_vedette-verify.git", which proves the target only (never the name itself when it is a CNAME: no TXT may sit beside a CNAME); null when _vedette-verify.<name> would pass 253 characters (no such name can exist)

path.description: /.well-known/vedette-verify.txt

content.description: The token: the whole content of the file

urls.description: The two addresses the box asks, http and https, on the IP

post.summary: Add a target (changes scan scope): a domain, or a public IPv4 address typed in. kind is domain or ip; left out, an IPv4 address is an IP and anything else a domain. A typed IP is accepted into the list at once and is never scanned, nor sent to Shodan, until it is proved: a token file at /.well-known/vedette-verify.txt on the IP (http or https, no redirect off the IP, the ACME HTTP-01 model), or forward-confirmed reverse DNS (its PTR is a name under a domain this box has proved, and that name resolves back to the IP). An A record of a proved domain pointing at the IP is not proof. The proof lasts 30 days and the box checks it again by itself (expires_at, next_check_at). 400 ip_not_allowed for a private, reserved or IPv6 address, 400 bad_value for an address on the Ignored list. The IP the box finds as its own egress address is added by detection, not here

get.summary: Compare two scan days: newly exposed, gone, changed

post.summary: Run OpenVAS again, on its own, for the newest scan of a public IP of this box, started less than 24 hours ago, whose OpenVAS step started and did not finish (stopped, cut by a restart, failed, or ended by OpenVAS before it found anything: findings it had are kept until a new deep scan). It checks the open TCP ports that scan found, and its outcome replaces that step in the same snapshot; the other results are kept. Answers at once with 202 and the run (openvas_only, phase greenbone); the page polls GET /exposure/scan and can stop it. The same refusals as Scan now come first (409 not_verified, expired, ip_not_current; 400 commitment_required when the target has no current commitment; 400 out_of_scope; 409 busy, also while OpenVAS runs; 429 rate_limited), then 400 bad_value for a domain (run its deep scan again), 409 nothing_to_rerun when the newest scan has no such step or started more than 24 hours ago, 503 scanner_unavailable when OpenVAS cannot scan now (off, starting, loading its feed, testing terms not accepted). Every attempt is audited as exposure.scan

by.description: Who pressed Scan now (an e-mail)

status.description: queued: a scan that waits for the box's one scan slot: the 202 answer of a Scan now behind another scan, and GET /exposure/scan when nothing ran since the box started and scans wait (the first of them; started_at is then when it was queued)

phase.description: queued: accepted, about to start; probing: the scan module's runner is scanning the target; saving: the result is being stored; greenbone: the snapshot of the other steps is stored and the optional Greenbone scan runs (up to 90 minutes), the box's one scan slot stays busy; done: the snapshot exists. A failed or stopped run keeps the phase it reached

snapshot_id.description: The new snapshot when status is done; also when a run was stopped during its Greenbone step, whose earlier results are kept

error.description: Why the run failed, in the same codes and texts the synchronous scan used (unreachable, too_many, module_off ...); null otherwise

stop_reason.description: Why the box stopped this run when it was not a person's Stop, e.g. "the testing terms of this target were withdrawn", "Vedette shut down"

openvas_only.description: The run is OpenVAS again for the newest scan of the target (POST /exposure/targets/{id}/openvas), not a scan: its phase is greenbone from the start

scheduled.description: The run is a scheduled scan of the target, started by the box

queue.description: The scans that wait after this one, in order; left out when none waits

by.description: Who pressed Scan now (an e-mail), or system for a scheduled scan

starting.description: Its checks run now (the TXT record, the proof, the box's IP): it is the next to run and can no longer be removed

phase.description: discovery: is the host up (ping or ARP); ports: port scan; services: service and version detection; scripts: nmap reads titles, certificates and NTLM answers; vulns: vulnerability checks (nuclei templates); web: passive web checks (ZAP); openvas: the optional OpenVAS deep scan; saving: the result is being stored

percent.description: How far into the phase, 0 to 100, one decimal; null when the tool gives no measure yet (show the phase without a bar)

done.description: With total: the count behind percent (unit says what is counted); null when the phase has no count

unit.description: checks: template x port pairs of the vulnerability checks; hosts: addresses of a discovery batch

started_at.description: When the job (the device, or the public IP scan) started: elapsed time is now minus this

phase_started_at.description: When the current phase (or the current pass of it: a device gets a second nmap pass over admin ports) started

updated_at.description: The latest report; nmap and nuclei report every 5 seconds at most, so an older one means the tool is quiet, not that the box hangs

eta.description: Estimated end of the current phase: nmap's own estimate for its phases, the pace so far for the vulnerability checks (after 10 s and 1 %); null until it can be estimated

ends_by.description: The latest time the current phase ends, when the box enforces a limit on it (the OpenVAS step: its 90-minute cap plus the time to stop the task and read what it found); null when none

message.description: A short English note on the pass, e.g. "Second pass: administration and alternative ports"; null when none

progress.description: How far the step that runs now is (#830): the port scan, service detection and vulnerability checks as the scan worker reports them, the passive web checks, and OpenVAS's own percent during the greenbone phase. Set while status is running; null otherwise

post.summary: Ask Shodan InternetDB what it has seen on this public IP. Only an administrator's click sends it: no job, no polling. Only a public IP of this box that is verified and still the one the box goes out through (the same check as before a scan, INV-13) is sent: 400 bad_value for a domain, 409 not_verified, expired or ip_not_current otherwise. One HTTPS GET of https://internetdb.shodan.io/<ip>, nothing else sent; 404 there is a normal answer (found false). At most one check a minute on the box (429 rate_limited); 502 unreachable when Shodan does not answer or its answer cannot be read. The answer is kept (one per IP) and every request sent is audited

delete.summary: Take the scan of this target that waits in the queue out of it (a Scan now or a scheduled scan). 409 not_queued when none waits, or its checks have started (stop it once it runs). Audited as exposure.scan

post.summary: Scan now. Answers at once with 202 and the run (ScanRun, status running): the scan itself goes on in the background and the page polls GET /exposure/scan. The checks below still answer synchronously. 409 when not verified, verification expired or the DNS TXT record is gone (re-checked right before the scan); 409 proof_missing when the proof of a typed IP is not found now (looked for again right before the scan); 409 ip_not_current when an IP is no longer the one the box goes out through (the latest check, or a fresh full check just before the scan, must see it); 400 commitment_required when the commitment is missing and the caller is an operator (an administrator must run the first scan). For an administrator that first scan IS the confirmation: it needs two-step sign-in on the account (403 twofa_required otherwise) and `notice_version` of the sentence shown next to the button (400 commitment_required when left out, 409 notice_changed when it is not the current one); the commitment is then recorded with who, when and that exact sentence, and the scan goes on. A target whose commitment is of the current sentence records nothing again; one of an older sentence is asked again once: it counts as missing (operators get 400 commitment_required "the confirmation text changed"), a request without notice_version gets 409 notice_changed, and the administrator's press replaces it. After those checks the scan module's runner does the scan (it follows this module's switch, so the Vulnerability scans module may be off): ports and pages are scanned on the box's own verified public IPs and on a typed public IP while its proof is found (looked for again right before, one live result reused for 5 minutes); a domain's names from certificate transparency, its MX and NS records and a list of common names (looked up through the box's DNS resolver) are listed with the kind of each address (INV-27) and get one GET of / by name on ports 80 and 443; the deep steps beyond that go to the box's own address, and to a typed IP or an address of a domain through the executors' own fence. 409 module_off while the External exposure module is off. While another scan runs on the box (or others wait) the scan waits in the box's queue: 202 with status queued and the queue, the checks above run again right before it starts, and GET /exposure/scan lists it until then (409 busy only for the target whose scan runs now). 429 rate_limited within 10 minutes of the target's last scan. Failures that come while the scan runs (400 too_many when the domain has more than 300 names in the logs; 502 unreachable when the certificate-transparency search (crt.sh) does not answer or the scan does not finish within 5 minutes; module_off when the module is switched off meanwhile) end the run as status failed with that code and text, and nothing is saved. Every attempt is audited

by.description: Who pressed Scan now (an e-mail)

status.description: queued: a scan that waits for the box's one scan slot: the 202 answer of a Scan now behind another scan, and GET /exposure/scan when nothing ran since the box started and scans wait (the first of them; started_at is then when it was queued)

phase.description: queued: accepted, about to start; probing: the scan module's runner is scanning the target; saving: the result is being stored; greenbone: the snapshot of the other steps is stored and the optional Greenbone scan runs (up to 90 minutes), the box's one scan slot stays busy; done: the snapshot exists. progress.description: How far the step that runs now is (#830): the port scan, service detection and vulnerability checks as the scan worker reports them, the passive web checks, and OpenVAS's own percent during the greenbone phase. Set while status is running; null otherwise

put.summary: Set how often the box scans this target by itself: off, daily, weekly (the default) or monthly, counted from the start of its newest scan. A scheduled scan runs as the box inside the scan window of Settings › Scanning › Safety, only while the ownership proof holds and the testing terms of the current version are accepted (else it is skipped and schedule.note says why), with the same steps as Deep scan now (OpenVAS only while it is turned on); it waits in the queue like any scan. What it finds new since the scan before (an open port, an admin page, a certificate now expiring within 30 days, an exploited vulnerability newly matched) goes to the alert channels. 400 bad_value for another value. Audited (exposure.schedule)

put.summary: Accept the testing terms of a verified target: every scan of it is then a deep scan; disruptive adds denial-of-service, password-guessing, default-password checks and exploit checks that send more than a harmless read (off by default). Admin with two-step sign-in (403 twofa_required); 409 notice_changed when version is not the current terms_notice.version; 409 not_verified, expired or ip_not_current (a paused IP); 409 shared_address for disruptive on an IP behind carrier-grade NAT (terms_warning). Lowering or withdrawing them stops a scan of this target that runs above the new level (ScanRun.stop_reason). Also records the Scan now commitment when the target has none of the current sentence. Accepting what is accepted changes nothing. Audited (exposure.terms_accept, with the flag)

post.summary: Re-check ownership: domain = DNS TXT record; typed IP = its token file, then reverse DNS (a pass renews it for 30 days; once every 30 seconds per target, and inside the box-wide bound of domain checks); IP the box found = the box must currently egress through this same IP (renews it for 30 days). Not found is a normal answer (verified:false). Rate limited: a domain once every 30 seconds per target, and a box-wide burst of 20 domain checks then one more every 10 seconds, the check of a name just added included (429 rate_limited says in how many seconds the next check is allowed), an IP within the 10 attempts an hour of the box. A domain already covered by the proof of another target of the box (a TXT record on its registered domain covers that name and the names under it) is verified with the message "Ownership already proven by the TXT record at example.com (checked 18 Nov 2026, 10:00)"

get.summary: Everything the box knows about a CVE (its brief) and your devices that match its exploited-list entry (404 not_in_data when the vulnerability data does not hold it)

description.description: NVD's English description, else the CNA's

display.description: The product in plain words: the exploited-list entry's, else the first of products

products.description: Vendor and product of the ranges that count ("vmware esxi"), sorted

nvd_status.description: NVD's vulnStatus ("Analyzed", "Deferred" …); null until NVD answered

record_read_at.description: When the CVE record was last read

name.description: MITRE's name; null for an id the CWE List does not hold

source.description: Who scored it: NVD, the CVE Numbering Authority (most often the vendor), or CISA (ADP)

privileges_required.description: For CVSS 2.0, its Authentication read the same way (none, single = low, multiple = high)

user_interaction.description: null for CVSS 2.0, which has no such metric

subsequent.description: CVSS 4.0 only: the impact on systems beyond the vulnerable one

summary.description: The reading in one sentence, for example "Attacker needs local access, low complexity, high privileges needed, no user action; high impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability; can reach beyond the vulnerable component."

anyOf.description: The CVSS vector read into words (confidentiality, integrity, availability: the impact on the vulnerable system; CVSS 2.0 partial = low, complete = high)

cvss.description: The one picked score: the newest CVSS version, NVD before the CNA before CISA; null when the CVE has no score

source.description: Who scored it: NVD, the CVE Numbering Authority (most often the vendor), or CISA (ADP)

scores.description: Every stored score, in the order the pick prefers them

list.description: "cisa", "vulncheck", or "custom:" followed by the id of a custom feed

source.description: The feed that holds the entry: "cisa-kev", "vulncheck-kev" or a custom feed id

source_name.description: That feed's name, as Settings -> Feeds shows it

lists.description: Its exploited-list entries, the one pages name first (CISA, VulnCheck, then custom lists)

kind.description: Why the CVE is urgent: "exploited" (an exploited list or a vendor says so), "public_exploit" (a public exploit or a scan template exists), and kinds new sources add

source.description: The feed that saw it ("cisa-kev", "metasploit", "nuclei-templates" …)

first_seen.description: When the source says it (its publication date), else when this box first saw it

qualifies.description: Passes the quality rule of its kind; a signal that does not is kept for its date only

origin.description: Who stated it: NVD, the CVE record's CNA (most often the vendor), or an ADP of the record

counts.description: The row the matcher reads: NVD's rows when NVD gives any, else the CVE record's

part.description: CPE part: a, o, h; "" for a CVE record row without a CPE

cpe.description: The CPE match criteria when the origin gave one, else ""

fixed.description: The release that fixes the range when the origin states one, else ""

version_type.description: The CVE record's versionType ("semver", "custom" …), else ""; "vendor:" and that word for a row kept in the vendor's own notation, which only the product's version scheme reads (it never counts)

default_status.description: A CVE record row's defaultStatus; "" for NVD's rows

versions.description: The versions in words: "from 2.0 before 2.4.58", "up to 3.1", "7.0 update_1", "every version"; in the version scheme's words when the product has one: "from 8.0 before 8.0 U3d (build 24585383)"

train.description: The release train the row's end belongs to, as the product's version scheme reads it ("8.0 U3"); "" when no scheme reads the row

fixed_release.description: The fixed release, as the product's version scheme reads it ("8.0 U3d (build 24585383)"); "" when none or no scheme reads the row

ranges.description: Every affected-versions row, the ones that count first

fixes.description: The fixed release of each product's release train, as its version scheme reads the ranges: the vendor's first, one per product and train; empty for a product without a scheme

ranges_from.description: The origin of the rows that count; null when there are none

ranges_complete.description: CVE record rows only: every product's list says what an unlisted version is

tags.description: The CVE record's tag words (NVD's are read into them: "Vendor Advisory" is vendor-advisory)

source.description: Who listed it: NVD, which tags every reference once it analyses the CVE, else the CVE record

group.description: The one group it is shown under: the first of the groups, in this order, that one of its tags names

references.description: Grouped: ordered by group, then by address

solution.description: The CNA's solution text; null when the record has none

workaround.description: The CNA's workaround text; null when the record has none

history.description: The days the box kept (CVEs on a list or with a signal), oldest first

hostname.description: The device's name: the name a person gave it in Vedette, else its host name; null when neither

matched.description: Devices whose product matches the exploited-list entry; null when the inventory is off or the CVE is on no exploited list

not_affected.description: devices that run the product but that the platform rules of the findings prove are not affected; left out of matched

published.description: NVD `published`; null when nvd-recent does not hold it (older than 12 months, or the feed is off)

regex.description: Optional regex; the first capture group (or the whole match) is kept

answered_by.description: The CISA list only: the copy the catalog on the box came from (newest from), "CISA" or "CISA GitHub mirror"; both copies are asked every check; null for every other feed and before the first good pull

state.description: The CISA list (cisa-kev) for the Home count: "off" when an admin turned it off, else "loaded" once a pull has ever succeeded (even if a later pull failed), else "never_loaded"

error.description: One line, cleaned: why the last pull failed (also when an earlier pull had loaded the list); null when the last pull worked, has not been tried, or the list is off

error.description: Why the last ask failed, one clause naming the copy ("cisa.gov refused this box (HTTP 403)"); null when it answered

catalog_version.description: The catalogVersion this copy last gave; null when not known yet

copies.description: What each copy of the CISA list said at its last check; empty for a list at an admin's own address or before the first check

get.summary: "This week, in short": plain-language sentences about products under attack

post.summary: Answer "I have it" (adds a manually declared device) or "Not relevant"

get.summary: List findings (CVE x device), optionally for one device

confidence.description: How sure the match is, 0 to 1. A finding its evidence confirms (a scan, the version the device itself reports, or a person) is at least 0.95 in any status, never below a scan's confirmation

basis.description: scan = confirmed by a scan template; person = confirmed by a person (an admin, with a note); version = the version is inside the affected range (confirmed when evidence.source says the device itself stated it, suspected otherwise); product = only the product matches

agent.description: the version compared is the one the device's own agent (osquery, Wazuh) reports installed: a detection, shown as "Detected by the agent", with nothing for the person to look up

agent_row.description: a product-only match on a software row the device's own agent reported with its installed version: Vedette could not compare that version with NVD's data, so the page does not ask to add the version

source.description: basis version only: the device itself stated the exact version (snmp: its answer to Vedette's SNMP read; agent: its own agent's OS or package list) and it is inside an affected range with an end, so the finding is confirmed by the version the device reports. Absent for a banner, an OS guess or a version a person typed

first_seen.description: When Vedette first matched this vulnerability to the device

last_seen.description: When Vedette last matched it: each re-match (after a change to the device's software, and every hour) or scan that still finds it moves it. Not when the device or its software was last seen; known_version.seen_at says when the version was reported

accepted_until.description: risk_accepted only: the last day of the acceptance (UTC); the finding reopens by itself after it

urgency.description: Why the finding matters now, most urgent first: 1 under attack here (an intrusion alert on this network named it), 2 exploited in the wild, 3 public exploit available, 4 critical on a device attackers target first, 5 update recommended (no sign of exploitation). Only 1 and 2 are "exploited"

name.description: The name the Devices page shows: hostname, else vendor and model, else the IP, else the software; never the internal id

ip.description: "—" when the device has no IP address

approved.description: false = "Device not added yet": nobody approved the device; its findings offer Add device (approve) and Ignore

ignored.description: a person ignored the device: its findings are hidden from the other tabs and listed under Ignored, with Restore

has_template.description: A safe vulnerability check exists for the CVE: the template pack the scan itself plans with has one (not the nuclei-templates feed flag), so a vulnerability check can confirm or rule it out

source.description: Which list the entry is on: texts and the source badge name it; an entry of VulnCheck KEV is never called CISA's

published.description: the day the CVE was published (NVD `published`), never the day CISA added it; null when NVD has not answered for it (then it counts as recent: an older CVE is not a finding on a product-only match, and a missing date never closes a finding)

kev.description: Read from KEV, not from the project recommendation pack

score.description: The CVSS base score (0.0 to 10.0, one decimal); its band follows from FIRST's table (3.x, 4.0) or NVD's v2 table (2.0: Low, Medium, High; no Critical)

version.description: The newest CVSS version NVD lists for the CVE with a usable score and vector (2.0 only when NVD has nothing newer)

source.description: nvd = NVD's own score ("Primary"); cna = another scorer NVD lists as "Secondary" (the CVE Numbering Authority or CISA's ADP), used only when NVD gives none for that version

vector.description: NVD's vector string of the score ("CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/…"; 2.0: "AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/…"): FIRST asks that a score be shown with its vector, so a score without a valid one is not shown

anyOf.description: #825 (findings INV-22, feeds INV-28): the CVSS base score from the same NVD records feeds already reads (nvd-kev, else nvd-recent). Shown next to the exploited status, never instead of it

cvss.description: null = no CVSS score known: the pages say "No score", never 0

resolution_reason.description: not_affected_version when Vedette closed the finding by itself (a matcher proof, or one of its rules that compares no version); null for a person's own action and for open findings. A string, not an enum: a new reason must not break the list

proved_version.description: A finding closed by proof (resolution_reason set): the version or package release the matcher compared to rule it out, as the device row gives it; null when the closure compared none (name only, age, an open platform question, another platform) or it is not closed by Vedette. An entry a person typed closed it only when this equals the entry

software_id.description: The device's software row the matcher matched the finding on (the id FindingRow.fix.group and ToFixAction use), stored when it opens, touches or closes the finding; "" until the next match reaches an older finding. Never guessed from the product

fix.description: GET /findings only, open findings: the update that fixes it with others; null when there is none to name

group.description: "<device id>/<software id>": the open findings with the same group are fixed by the same update

kind.description: fixed = the device version is inside a range that ends before `fixed`, and `fixed` is outside every range that applies; up_to = inside a range whose end `fixed` is itself affected (no fixed release named); end_listed = inside a range that ends before `fixed`, but NVD lists releases of `fixed` itself as affected (Junos: "before 20.4", then 20.4R1 … one by one): `fixed` is not a fix, the vendor advisory names it; branches = the version is unknown or unreadable, `branches` lists the fix of each release line; distro = a package of the distribution, whose security updates carry the fix under their own numbers: an agent read it from the device's package database (deb, rpm or apk), a person gave its package release (an apk, Debian or RPM release, or any release on a device that runs a Linux distribution), or the version carries a marker such as ubuntu, +deb12, .el9; feature_update = a Windows release NVD does not list for the fix, which only a later release of its line (`branches[0].branch`, from build `fixed`) has: Microsoft no longer updates it, so it needs a feature update; esu = the fixing Windows build `fixed` comes only with Extended Security Updates for `branches[0].branch`

accepted_until.description: risk_accepted only: the last day of the acceptance (UTC); the finding reopens by itself after it

urgency.description: Why the finding matters now, most urgent first: 1 under attack here (an intrusion alert on this network named it), 2 exploited in the wild, 3 public exploit available, 4 critical on a device attackers target first, 5 update recommended (no sign of exploitation). Only 1 and 2 are "exploited"

name.description: The name the Devices page shows: hostname, else vendor and model, else the IP, else the software; never the internal id

ip.description: "—" when the device has no IP address

approved.description: false = "Device not added yet": nobody approved the device; its findings offer Add device (approve) and Ignore

ignored.description: a person ignored the device: its findings are hidden from the other tabs and listed under Ignored, with Restore

has_template.description: A safe vulnerability check exists for the CVE: the template pack the scan itself plans with has one (not the nuclei-templates feed flag), so a vulnerability check can confirm or rule it out

source.description: Which list the entry is on: texts and the source badge name it; an entry of VulnCheck KEV is never called CISA's

published.description: the day the CVE was published (NVD `published`), never the day CISA added it; null when NVD has not answered for it (then it counts as recent: an older CVE is not a finding on a product-only match, and a missing date never closes a finding)

kev.description: Read from KEV, not from the project recommendation pack

score.description: The CVSS base score (0.0 to 10.0, one decimal); its band follows from FIRST's table (3.x, 4.0) or NVD's v2 table (2.0: Low, Medium, High; no Critical)

version.description: The newest CVSS version NVD lists for the CVE with a usable score and vector (2.0 only when NVD has nothing newer)

source.description: nvd = NVD's own score ("Primary"); cna = another scorer NVD lists as "Secondary" (the CVE Numbering Authority or CISA's ADP), used only when NVD gives none for that version

vector.description: NVD's vector string of the score ("CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/…"; 2.0: "AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/…"): FIRST asks that a score be shown with its vector, so a score without a valid one is not shown

anyOf.description: #825 (findings INV-22, feeds INV-28): the CVSS base score from the same NVD records feeds already reads (nvd-kev, else nvd-recent). Shown next to the exploited status, never instead of it

cvss.description: null = no CVSS score known: the pages say "No score", never 0

resolution_reason.description: not_affected_version when Vedette closed the finding by itself (a matcher proof, or one of its rules that compares no version); null for a person's own action and for open findings. A string, not an enum: a new reason must not break the list

proved_version.description: A finding closed by proof (resolution_reason set): the version or package release the matcher compared to rule it out, as the device row gives it; null when the closure compared none (name only, age, an open platform question, another platform) or it is not closed by Vedette. An entry a person typed closed it only when this equals the entry

software_id.description: The device's software row the matcher matched the finding on (the id FindingRow.fix.group and ToFixAction use), stored when it opens, touches or closes the finding; "" until the next match reaches an older finding. Never guessed from the product

fix.description: GET /findings only, open findings: the update that fixes it with others; null when there is none to name

group.description: "<device id>/<software id>": the open findings with the same group are fixed by the same update

kind.description: fixed = upgrade to `fixed` (a Windows release: the monthly cumulative update with build `fixed` or later); esu = that build needs Extended Security Updates; feature_update = no update of this release fixes them, move to release `fixed`; distro = install the distribution's security updates for the package

windows.description: A Windows release row: the update is the monthly cumulative update Windows Update offers

software.description: Display name of the software row

version.description: The installed version

fixed.description: The release or build that fixes them all; feature_update: the release to move to; empty for distro

distro.description: distro: "Ubuntu" or "Debian", empty for the distribution's

pro.description: distro: the fix of at least one of them is in Ubuntu Pro (ESM) only

anyOf.description: one update fixes this finding together with the device's other open findings of the same software (top-tier: one item per missing update)

software.description: Display name of the software the finding was matched on

source.description: Who gave the version: the device's agent, its answer to Vedette's SNMP read, its own statement on the network (LLDP), a network scan, or a person on the Devices page

seen_at.description: When that source last gave the version: the agent's last list, the last scan or SNMP read that returned it, or when a person entered it; null when not known. Not the same as the finding's last_seen

known_version.description: Null when the matched software has no version or its source is not known

suspected_why.description: A suspected finding only: why it is not confirmed and what would confirm it, in words (who stated the version, whether a vulnerability check exists for the CVE and whether the scan reaches the device); null for any other status

fixed.description: The fixed release (fixed), the last affected release (up_to), the upstream fixed release as a reference when NVD names one (distro: the backport may keep the package's number below it); empty for branches

branch.description: Release line such as 7.4; empty when it cannot be told

more.description: Release lines with a fix left out of branches

no_fix.description: Release lines NVD gives no fixed release for (a range that ends at an affected version)

distro.description: "Ubuntu" or "Debian" when the device runs one, empty otherwise. distro: whose security updates to install (empty = the distribution). id.description: The software line of the device (inventory)

name.description: Display name, as on the device page

version.description: The version the match compared

status.description: under_attack = someone on your network sent this exploit and this device is affected (layer 1); exploited = attackers use it in real attacks (layer 2); public_exploit = working exploit code is public (layer 3); critical_edge = critical, no login needed, on a device class attackers target first (layer 4); update_recommended = a known flaw, no sign of exploitation yet (layer 5); patched, mitigated, accepted, not_relevant, false_positive = handled, as the handling resolution says

layer.description: The most urgent layer that applies; the open status is OPEN_FINDING_STATUSES[layer - 1]

since.description: When the finding entered this layer

source.description: The signal source: cisa-kev, msrc, chrome, cisco, fortinet, apple, android, rapid7, gti, nuclei, metasploit, exploit-db, github-poc; ids for an attack seen here (layer 1); cvss for layer 4 (computed)

name.description: The source as people name it: "CISA KEV", "Rapid7", "GitHub"

date.description: When the source said so (or the box first saw it say so); layer 1: the newest alert; layer 4: since when the rule holds

detail.description: A short fact of the signal: "244 stars" for a public exploit, the attacker address for layer 1; null when none

due.description: Layer 2: the day the list asks for the fix (CISA KEV due date); null otherwise

items.description: One urgency layer that applies, with its evidence

reasons.description: Every layer 1 to 4 that applies, most urgent first, each source its own entry; empty for layer 5. The GUI says "not yet in CISA KEV" for a layer 2 without a cisa-kev entry

internet.description: "Reachable from the Internet (seen <date>)": the day an exposure scan last saw the affected service from outside; raises the order inside a layer, never the layer

urgency.description: Kept while handled: the layer the finding had

anyOf.description: The CVSS base score of the CVE and its band (the score the catalogue picks for it). Never changes the status. null = "Not scored yet", never 0

verified.description: no = not confirmed yet; device = the device itself reports the affected version (agent, SNMP, package list); scan = a safe check confirmed it; person = a person confirmed it

basis.description: What the match rests on: scan = a safe check; device_version = a version the device itself reports; package = a distribution package release; banner_version = a version read from a network banner; statement = a version a person typed for the device; person = a person said it is affected

by.description: verified person: who confirmed it

at.description: When it was confirmed; null while not confirmed

verification.description: The second line under the status: "Confirmed by a safe check", "Confirmed: the device reports this version", "Confirmed by <user>", "Not confirmed yet: based on a scan banner"

resolution.description: patched = the fixed version is installed or the software is gone; mitigated = a workaround is in place, the flaw is still in the software; accepted = a person decided to live with it until a day; not_relevant = it does not apply to this device; false_positive = the match was wrong

via.description: How it was handled: person = a person marked it; version_moved = the software moved past the affected version (from_version, to_version); software_removed = the software is gone; distro_fixed = the distribution says the installed package is fixed; scan_clear = a safe check that had matched came back clear; data_corrected = no longer detected while nothing on the device changed (the match was corrected: never patch credit); not_installed = a person said the software is not installed

by.description: "system" when Vedette handled it; else the person

accepted_until.description: accepted: the last day; the finding reopens by itself after it. null otherwise

from_version.description: via version_moved: the version that was affected

to_version.description: via version_moved: the version now installed

anyOf.description: Who and how, from stored fields: "Patched by Vedette: version moved 6.24 → 7.23 (18 Nov)", "Mitigated by <user> (17 Nov): <note>"

why.description: still_detected = a person marked it patched and a newer reading still shows the affected version; detected_again = it came back after Vedette closed it; acceptance_expired = the accepted risk reached its last day

at.description: still_detected, detected_again: the time of the reading; acceptance_expired: when it reopened

anyOf.description: An open finding that was handled before: the line that says why it is open again

reopened.description: null unless the finding is open again after a handling

key.description: The "By fix" group (the same key on every device the same fix applies to); opaque

kind.description: update = install `version` of the software or later; distro_update = install the distribution's package release `version` or later; os_update = install the operating system update `ref` (a KB number) or build `version`; feature_update = no update of this release fixes it, move to release `version`; none_yet = the vendor has no fix yet (`url` is the advisory); unknown = no fix data

product.description: The product the fix is for, as people name it ("OpenSSH")

version.description: update, distro_update, feature_update: the version or release to install; os_update: the build when known

ref.description: os_update: the KB number; none_yet: the advisory id when known

version.description: The newest CVSS version NVD lists for the CVE with a usable score and vector (2.0 only when NVD has nothing newer)

source.description: nvd = NVD's own score ("Primary"); cna = another scorer NVD lists as "Secondary" (the CVE Numbering Authority or CISA's ADP), used only when NVD gives none for that version

status.description: under_attack = someone on your network sent this exploit and this device is affected (layer 1); exploited = attackers use it in real attacks (layer 2); public_exploit = working exploit code is public (layer 3); critical_edge = critical, no login needed, on a device class attackers target first (layer 4); update_recommended = a known flaw, no sign of exploitation yet (layer 5); patched, mitigated, accepted, not_relevant, false_positive = handled, as the handling resolution says

layer.description: The most urgent layer that applies; the open status is OPEN_FINDING_STATUSES[layer - 1]

since.description: When the finding entered this layer

source.description: The signal source: cisa-kev, msrc, chrome, cisco, fortinet, apple, android, rapid7, gti, nuclei, metasploit, exploit-db, github-poc; ids for an attack seen here (layer 1); cvss for layer 4 (computed)

name.description: The source as people name it: "CISA KEV", "Rapid7", "GitHub"

date.description: When the source said so (or the box first saw it say so); layer 1: the newest alert; layer 4: since when the rule holds

detail.description: A short fact of the signal: "244 stars" for a public exploit, the attacker address for layer 1; null when none

due.description: Layer 2: the day the list asks for the fix (CISA KEV due date); null otherwise

items.description: One urgency layer that applies, with its evidence

reasons.description: Every layer 1 to 4 that applies, most urgent first, each source its own entry; empty for layer 5. The GUI says "not yet in CISA KEV" for a layer 2 without a cisa-kev entry

internet.description: "Reachable from the Internet (seen <date>)": the day an exposure scan last saw the affected service from outside; raises the order inside a layer, never the layer

urgency.description: Kept while handled: the layer the finding had

anyOf.description: The CVSS base score of the CVE and its band (the score the catalogue picks for it). Never changes the status. null = "Not scored yet", never 0

verified.description: no = not confirmed yet; device = the device itself reports the affected version (agent, SNMP, package list); scan = a safe check confirmed it; person = a person confirmed it

basis.description: What the match rests on: scan = a safe check; device_version = a version the device itself reports; package = a distribution package release; banner_version = a version read from a network banner; statement = a version a person typed for the device; person = a person said it is affected

by.description: verified person: who confirmed it

at.description: When it was confirmed; null while not confirmed

verification.description: The second line under the status: "Confirmed by a safe check", "Confirmed: the device reports this version", "Confirmed by <user>", "Not confirmed yet: based on a scan banner"

resolution.description: patched = the fixed version is installed or the software is gone; mitigated = a workaround is in place, the flaw is still in the software; accepted = a person decided to live with it until a day; not_relevant = it does not apply to this device; false_positive = the match was wrong

via.description: How it was handled: person = a person marked it; version_moved = the software moved past the affected version (from_version, to_version); software_removed = the software is gone; distro_fixed = the distribution says the installed package is fixed; scan_clear = a safe check that had matched came back clear; data_corrected = no longer detected while nothing on the device changed (the match was corrected: never patch credit); not_installed = a person said the software is not installed

why.description: still_detected = a person marked it patched and a newer reading still shows the affected version; detected_again = it came back after Vedette closed it; acceptance_expired = the accepted risk reached its last day

at.description: still_detected, detected_again: the time of the reading; acceptance_expired: when it reopened

since.description: When the finding entered this layer

source.description: The signal source: cisa-kev, msrc, chrome, cisco, fortinet, apple, android, rapid7, gti, nuclei, metasploit, exploit-db, github-poc; ids for an attack seen here (layer 1); cvss for layer 4 (computed)

name.description: The source as people name it: "CISA KEV", "Rapid7", "GitHub"

date.description: When the source said so (or the box first saw it say so); layer 1: the newest alert; layer 4: since when the rule holds

resolution.description: patched = the fixed version is installed or the software is gone; mitigated = a workaround is in place, the flaw is still in the software; accepted = a person decided to live with it until a day; not_relevant = it does not apply to this device; false_positive = the match was wrong

fixed.description: fixed: the version that fixes every CVE of the item; windows, esu: the build of the cumulative update; distro: the distribution's package version that fixes every CVE of the item on the device's release

kind.description: fixed = upgrade the software to `fixed`; distro = a distribution's package, judged by the distribution's own fix data (`distro_data`), never moved to an upstream release; windows = the monthly cumulative update with build `fixed` or later; esu = the same on a Windows release past its end of support: the update comes only with Extended Security Updates

distro_data.description: kind distro: fixed = upgrade the source package `software` from `version` to the distribution's fixed release `fixed` or later (Ubuntu, Debian, Alpine data); no_fix = the distribution's data says these CVEs have no fix from it yet (`distro` names it): nothing to install yet; none = the distribution's data has no word on the package (Red Hat, SUSE and others Vedette reads no data for, a package the data never names, another build): NVD lists these CVEs for its upstream version, so the page says to check `distro`'s security updates, never that an update fixes them. "" for every other kind

pro.description: distro only: `fixed` is in Ubuntu Pro (ESM) only; false otherwise

distro.description: distro with `fixed` empty (distro_data no_fix or none): the distribution ("Alpine Linux", "Ubuntu", "Debian"); empty for "the distribution's" and for every other kind

nvd_lag.description: windows, esu: `fixed` is the newest monthly update Microsoft's release information lists for the release, newer than the update that carries every fixed build NVD names for these CVEs. The item fixes at least `cves`; the newest update's CVEs are not yet analysed by NVD, so the page says "at least". false otherwise

kb.description: windows, esu: the KB number of `fixed` when Microsoft's release information lists that build ("KB5131080"), named next to the build; "" otherwise

tier.description: likely = EPSS 10 % or more; recent = published in the last 12 months; a CVE on an exploited list is a finding, never here

basis.description: Evidence: scan = a scan engine (nuclei, OpenVAS, ZAP) found it on the device; agent = the device's agent reports a build or package inside the affected range; distro = Ubuntu's or Debian's own data says the installed package is affected; version = an exact version compared with the CVE's ranges. Never a product-only match

severity.description: NVD's CVSS severity; null when NVD has not scored it yet

published.description: NVD `published`; older than 12 months only with basis scan

cves.description: Likely first, by EPSS; then the recent ones by CVSS score, then EPSS; then newest. Empty only for a Windows release below the newest monthly update Microsoft lists for it while no CVE NVD has analysed gives the device an item (kind windows or esu): the item names the update, lists under All and Recent, and ranks after every item with a CVE; nvd_lag is true while the update is under six weeks old ("its CVEs are not yet analysed by NVD"), false after ("NVD lists no CVE of it for this release yet")

agent_gone.description: A CVE of the item rests on an agent's row and no agent of this box reports the device now (agent-intake off, no agent bound, the agent silent past its stale limit; the same answer as the finding page's "No agent reports" line): `version` is the last one an agent reported

agent_reported.description: With agent_gone: the day the agent last reported the row (YYYY-MM-DD); null otherwise or when not known

by.description: Who marked it done

note.description: The note they gave; "" when none

version.description: The version of the software when it was marked: the mark holds while the device reports this version and no new CVE joins the item

done.description: Always null: a recommended update a person installed is Patched on its findings
Items a person marked done (whatever tier), listed with ?done=true

counts.description: The number of items each tier filter lists, for the same device filter, whatever tier was asked: one answer gives every tab its count

unchecked_devices.description: Devices with no version Vedette can read: not checked

old_evidence.description: CVEs published more than 12 months ago listed because a scan engine found them

recent.description: Feed nvd-recent (tier 3, and the published dates of tier 2)

recent_since.description: CVEs published on or after this day are in the data (12 months back)

get.summary: osquery install script for Windows Server, served by the box; public, contains no secrets; 404 no_box_address while the box knows no address other machines can reach

One-line osquery install script for Linux (Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux; x86_64 or arm64), served by the box; public, contains no secrets (the token is passed as a parameter); 404 no_box_address while the box knows no address other machines can reach

The official osquery packages and SHA256SUMS the box ships (osquery_<v>-1.linux_amd64.deb, osquery-<v>-1.linux.x86_64.rpm, osquery_<v>-1.linux_arm64.deb, osquery-<v>-1.linux.aarch64.rpm, osquery-<v>.msi), so servers need no Internet; public, no secret, any other name is 404
The certificate osquery pins to trust this box (PEM, public, no secret); the install script embeds the same text

post.summary: osquery config (machine to machine): the read-only snapshot schedule for an enrolled node; node_invalid: true makes osquery enroll again
osquery enrollment (machine to machine): exchanges a valid enrollment token for a node key; node_invalid: true when the token is unknown, revoked or expired

enroll_secret.description: The enrollment token (osquery reads it from enroll_secret_path)

node_key.description: Returned once, only when enrollment succeeds; osquery sends it with every later call

post.summary: osquery logger (machine to machine): results of the scheduled queries from an enrolled node; they update the inventory with source agent

data.description: Events: scheduled-query snapshots (result) or osquery own log lines (status, read for size and dropped)

post.summary: The install script asks "has THIS machine enrolled yet" (body: its host_identifier; empty body = token-wide counts only); token goes in the Authorization: Bearer header, never in the URL

host_identifier.description: The name this machine enrols under (the install script sets osquery host_identifier = specified and sends the same name here); the install script sends it so the answer is about THIS machine

host_last_seen.description: Only when host_identifier was sent: when the box last heard from the machine of this token with that name (a hostname match ignores case), null when no machine of the token has enrolled under it; absent when no usable host_identifier was sent. It tells nothing about machines of other tokens

get.summary: Issued osquery tokens and the Wazuh connection (if any)

sha256.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the script served by the box; users compare it before running

script.description: Full script text, for the admin to read first

sha256.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the script served by the box; users compare it before running

script.description: Full script text, for the admin to read first

file.description: File name; the browser downloads it from /api/v1/install/osquery/{file}

sha256.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) from the box's SHA256SUMS, which the core build writes from deploy/osquery/PINS

packages.description: The osquery packages this box serves; empty when it has no copy (a development build without the mirror)

created_by.description: Who made it (null for a token made before this was kept)

expires_at.description: When it stops enrolling machines. null = never; default 7 days once a machine has enrolled; a token no machine enrolled with expires 24 hours after it was made. The token only enrolls osquery (it can read nothing) and can be revoked

device_id.description: The device it was made for (its agent row offers Show setup); null = any machine

host.description: The name the machine enrolled under

state.description: reporting = it called within three of its rhythm (rhythm_s); quiet = it did not (quiet_since is its last call); never_reported = it calls but has delivered no result since it enrolled, after the first hour; replaced = a newer agent of the same machine (same name, any token) took over, so this record is only left to remove

last_seen.description: Its last call to the box (config or results)

last_result_at.description: Its last delivered result log; null = none yet

quiet_since.description: state quiet: when it was last heard; null otherwise

rhythm_s.description: The interval it is judged by, in seconds: the longer of how often it was told to call (osquery: its 5-minute config refresh; the package reporter: its hourly run) and how often it really calls. Quiet after three of it

nodes.description: Every enrolled osquery agent, the quiet ones first, then by name

server_url.description: https://<box IP>:8443, or https://<VEDETTE_BOX_IP>:8443 when the IP is unknown

url.description: Wazuh server API address, e.g. https://wazuh-manager:55000

password_last4.description: Password is stored encrypted; only the last 4 characters

get.summary: Which agent of this box reads the device and whether an ask to send its software now is open ("I updated it", S-MIT-1). 404 not_found: no such device; 404 too while agent-intake is off

agent.description: osquery = an osquery agent enrolled with this box reports on the device: Vedette can ask it to send its software now; wazuh = only the Wazuh pull reads it: Vedette cannot ask, the next pull brings the list; none = no agent of this box reads it now; box = the Vedette box itself, which reads its own packages every hour

asked_at.description: The open ask: when a person asked the osquery agent to send its software now, until its list (built with its OS answer: kernel_info, os_revision) arrives or 15 minutes pass; null when none is open

ask_again_at.description: agent osquery: when a new ask is possible (10 minutes after the last one) while that is still ahead; null otherwise

last_seen.description: agent osquery: when the agent last called the box (config or results); agent wazuh: when a pull last delivered the device; null otherwise

state.description: agent osquery or wazuh: reporting, quiet (silent for more than three of its rhythm: show "quiet since quiet_since" and, for osquery, the command to check the service) or never_reported (osquery); null for the other agents

quiet_since.description: state quiet: when the agent last called the box; null otherwise

rhythm_s.description: agent osquery or wazuh: the interval its state is judged by, in seconds (osquery: the longer of its config refresh and how often it really calls; wazuh: the pull interval); null otherwise

off.description: A person turned the agent off for this device: its data is refused and it cannot be asked (409 agent_off)

post.summary: I updated it: ask the device's osquery agent to send its software now. For 15 minutes, or until its list arrives, the box's config gives the agent's software queries (the same read-only queries, nothing else) a 60 s interval; osquery reads its config every 5 minutes. post.summary: Ignore a device that needs no watching, such as a staff phone, or stop ignoring it. Ignored: it stays known (seen again by its MAC or agent, it is the same device) but leaves To review and the Devices list, its new-device alert closes, its network scan and SNMP reads turn off and its open findings close as not relevant ("Closed by Vedette: the device was ignored by <person>.", no notice; findings a person settled keep their status); a trap hit or an intrusion-detection incident from it still alerts. Stopped: it goes back to To review (not approved), its own scan and SNMP settings apply again (they are kept while it is ignored), the findings Ignore closed reopen, matched again. Saying it again changes nothing. 404 not_found. 409 box_device: the Vedette box itself
