get.summary: The device's sources as three rows (network scan, SNMP, agent): each with its state, colour, last time it read the device, switch and one button, decided on the server. 404 not_found

state.description: module_off: the module behind the source is off. no_address: the device has no address to send to (scan, snmp). off: a person turned the source off for this device. waiting: on, nothing read yet (scan: the first check is the next scan window's; snmp: set up, no read yet). working: the scan read the device, or SNMP answers. not_approved: SNMP reads approved devices only. not_set_up: no SNMP settings for this device. not_answering: the last SNMP read got no answer. none: no agent of this box reads the device. reporting: the agent reports on its rhythm (osquery by its own calls, Wazuh by its pull, the box by its own hourly list). quiet: an agent (osquery or Wazuh) silent for more than three of its own rhythm (rhythm_s of the agents list), the same rule everywhere. Agent row: waiting = a token was made for this device and no agent reads it yet; off = a person turned the agent off for this device. never_reported: enrolled, never sent its data. replaced: a newer enrolment of the same machine took over. unavailable: the module could not say just now. box: the Vedette box itself, which reads its own packages and ports and is not scanned or read over SNMP (no switch, no button). ignored: a person ignored the device: the box does not scan or read it until they stop ignoring it (no switch, no button)

dot.description: green: working or reporting; amber: quiet or never reported; red: SNMP not answering; grey: everything else (off, not set up, waiting, module off)

last_at.description: When the source last read the device: the newest scan result (observation, open port, software banner); SNMP's last answer; the agent's last call (osquery) or its newest data (Wazuh, the box). null when never

switch.description: The person's switch of this source for this device (PUT /inventory/devices/{id}/sources); null when the row has none: SNMP before it is set up, an agent row with no agent (unless it is off), the box itself and an ignored device

anyOf.description: The one button of the row. turn_on_module: the module is off. scan_now: check the device now instead of at the next window. approve: approve the device (SNMP reads approved devices only). set_up: set up SNMP for this device (PUT /inventory/snmp/devices/{id}). check_now: SNMP Check now (POST /inventory/snmp/devices/{id}/check). create_token: no agent reads the device and no token was made for it: create an agent token for it (POST /inventory/agents/tokens with device_id). show_setup: a token was made for this device and no agent reads it yet, or its agent enrolled and never reported: show the token (the row's token) and the install command again. check: the agent reported at least once: the troubleshooting steps

action.description: null when the row offers no button

agent.description: Agent row: which agent of this box reads the device (box = the Vedette box itself, which reads its own packages); null on the other rows

created_by.description: Who made it (null for a token made before this was kept)

expires_at.description: When it stops enrolling machines. null = never; default 7 days once a machine has enrolled; a token no machine enrolled with expires 24 hours after it was made. The token only enrolls osquery (it can read nothing) and can be revoked

device_id.description: The device it was made for (its agent row offers Show setup); null = any machine

token.description: Agent row: the token Show setup shows: the token its osquery agent enrolled with, else the newest token made for this device that still enrolls machines (the secret is never here: it is shown once, when the token is made); administrators only (the tokens list is theirs): null for the other roles, and on the other rows

only.description: What feeds the device when none of the rows does: passive = only heard on the network ("Seen passively"), manual = only what a person entered ("Added by hand"); null otherwise

put.summary: Turn the network scan, the SNMP reads or the agents' data of one device on or off. On is the person's consent to that traffic: a device added by hand gets it from then on, inside every other safety rule (scope, exclusions, window, fragile, never scan); turning the network scan on queues the device for the next window. Off stops it for any device (the run on it stops); what the source found stays and manual values still win. Agent off: every agent's data for the device is refused and what the agents read stops counting (their software readings and open ports go); on: taken again, and an osquery agent is asked to send its software now. One audit row per source changed. 400 bad_source: neither, or not on/off. 404 not_found. 409 box_device: the Vedette box itself. 409 device_ignored: turning a source on for an ignored device

agent.description: The agents' data of this device (osquery, Wazuh). off: every agent's data for it is refused and what they read stops counting (its software readings and open ports of the agents go); on: taken again, and an osquery agent is asked to send its software now

get.summary: Every run of every engine, newest first: LAN sweeps, device checks, SNMP reads, vulnerability checks, exposure scans and their engine steps. lan_ranges.description: Internal IPv4 CIDR (RFC 1918 or 100.64.0.0/10); inventory lan_ranges

items.description: 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday

days.description: Empty only on a box whose discovery was saved off without a day; a save needs one

to.description: Earlier than from: crosses midnight

time_zone.description: IANA zone the window is read in (the organization time zone); read-only

window.description: One window for discovery, version scans, SNMP rounds, scheduled vulnerability checks and the scheduled scans of public targets. Scan now and Check this device now are not bound by it

requests_per_s.description: nuclei on LAN devices (was scan config rate)

exclusions.description: IPv4 or CIDR never touched by any engine on the LAN (a merge of two old lists may hold more than the 200 a save accepts)

kinds.description: Types scanned once, gently, when first seen; passive-only after that

regular_scan_kinds.description: Subset of kinds that may still get regular scans

devices.description: Devices fragile today (by type or marked by hand), for the link to Devices with the fragile filter; read-only

version.description: Names the stored values of this block (#860): PUT /scanning/safety must send back the version it was built on (409 safety_changed otherwise), so a page opened before an inline add never drops it. Every answer that changed the block carries the new one. The same values give the same version

module.description: The module it belongs to; PATCH /modules/{id} of that module still works

can_toggle.description: false: it has no switch of its own; follows names the engine whose switch it obeys, or reason says why

follows.description: nmap-versions and snmp follow nmap-discovery; null otherwise

affects.description: Engines that stop too when this one is turned off (osquery and wazuh share the agent-intake switch; nmap-discovery off stops nmap-versions and the SNMP rounds). External scans (zap, openvas) follow the External exposure module, not nuclei. The page names them before turning off

state.description: off: switched off (or its module is); needs_setup: on, but it has nothing to work with yet (scope not confirmed, no SNMP credential, no osquery token, no Wazuh server, no verified target, no Trap IP); starting: its container is starting, or OpenVAS loads its feed; ready: on and waiting for its window, schedule or a person; running: a job runs now; error: it failed and needs a person (reason says what); unavailable: this box cannot run it (container-only install, tool missing, not enough memory)

reason.description: Plain sentence for needs_setup, starting, error and unavailable, or a warning while ready (e.g. "A sweep of these ranges needs 3 windows"); null otherwise

preview.description: Its module ships as Preview in v1 (scan, honeypot)

ram_mb.description: Memory it may take, from a fact of the box's code: its container's memory cap (sensor 512, honeypot 256, scan 1024, ZAP 1024), or the measured peak for OpenVAS (about 4000); 0 for osquery and Wazuh, which run inside core. null when it is not known; never an estimate

while.description: on: held as long as the engine is on (a long-running container); running: only while one of its jobs runs (a one-shot container, or OpenVAS scanning)

container.description: The container it shares with other engines (scan: nmap, SNMP and nuclei); count a shared container once. null when the figure is its own

text.description: One sentence from the box, e.g. "Swept 254 addresses, 3 new devices", "Last report from an osquery agent", "Last trap hit"

next_run_at.description: Next window opening (nmap-discovery, nmap-versions, snmp), next scheduled scan (nuclei), next Wazuh sync; null for engines that listen all the time (passive, osquery, honeypot) or run only when a person asks (zap, openvas)

engines.description: Every engine of this version, in display order; post-v1 ones (credentialed scans) are not listed

id.description: The run: a scan_run id, an exposure ScanRun id, an sa_job id, or a run of POST /scanning/engines/nmap-discovery/run

target_id.description: The device id or exposure target id the run is about, for a link; null for a sweep or several devices

phase.description: discovery: is the host up (ping or ARP); ports: port scan; services: service and version detection; scripts: nmap reads titles, certificates and NTLM answers; vulns: vulnerability checks (nuclei templates); web: passive web checks (ZAP); openvas: the optional OpenVAS deep scan; saving: the result is being stored

percent.description: How far into the phase, 0 to 100, one decimal; null when the tool gives no measure yet (show the phase without a bar)

done.description: With total: the count behind percent (unit says what is counted); null when the phase has no count

unit.description: checks: template x port pairs of the vulnerability checks; hosts: addresses of a discovery batch

started_at.description: When the job (the device, or the public IP scan) started: elapsed time is now minus this

phase_started_at.description: When the current phase (or the current pass of it: a device gets a second nmap pass over admin ports) started

updated_at.description: The latest report; nmap and nuclei report every 5 seconds at most, so an older one means the tool is quiet, not that the box hangs

eta.description: Estimated end of the current phase: nmap's own estimate for its phases, the pace so far for the vulnerability checks (after 10 s and 1 %); null until it can be estimated

ends_by.description: The latest time the current phase ends, when the box enforces a limit on it (the OpenVAS step: its 90-minute cap plus the time to stop the task and read what it found); null when none

message.description: A short English note on the pass, e.g. "Second pass: administration and alternative ports"; null when none

progress.description: null until the run reports a step, and for runs that do not report one

running.description: Jobs running now across engines, for the "1 scan running" indicator of the top bar

memory_mb.description: MemTotal of the box; null when it cannot be read (container-only install may report its limit)

reserved_mb.description: Sum of the cost of the engines that hold memory now (while on, plus while running for running jobs), a shared container counted once, plus core's 2048

patch.summary: Turn an engine on or off: its module switch (passive, osquery, wazuh, nuclei, honeypot), active discovery (nmap-discovery: on turns sensor-active on first when with_dependencies is set, off never turns the module off) or the OpenVAS flag (openvas). Audited by the switch it moves. 409 not_toggleable (nmap-versions, snmp, zap), missing_dependencies, not_appliance, module_off (openvas while External exposure is off), low_memory, low_disk; 400 no_ranges, no_days, scope_not_confirmed (nmap-discovery on, checked before anything moves), core_module. Returns the whole page, since one switch can change several engines

with_dependencies.description: As PATCH /modules/{id}: also turn on the modules it needs instead of 409 missing_dependencies

container.description: The container it shares with other engines (scan: nmap, SNMP and nuclei); count a shared container once. null when the figure is its own

text.description: One sentence from the box, e.g. "Swept 254 addresses, 3 new devices", "Last report from an osquery agent", "Last trap hit"

next_run_at.description: Next window opening (nmap-discovery, nmap-versions, snmp), next scheduled scan (nuclei), next Wazuh sync; null for engines that listen all the time (passive, osquery, honeypot) or run only when a person asks (zap, openvas)

engines.description: Every engine of this version, in display order; post-v1 ones (credentialed scans) are not listed

id.description: The run: a scan_run id, an exposure ScanRun id, an sa_job id, or a run of POST /scanning/engines/nmap-discovery/run

target_id.description: The device id or exposure target id the run is about, for a link; null for a sweep or several devices

running.description: Jobs running now across engines, for the "1 scan running" indicator of the top bar

post.summary: Scan the LAN now (no targets: a sweep of the whole scope, then the scans of the devices it queued) or check these devices now (targets), whatever the window, for at most one hour (devices not reached by then wait for the window). Audited before anything is sent (scanning.run: the run id and the ranges or devices; no audit row, no run). Runs in the background: the answer is the run, which GET /scanning lists in running[] with its progress until it ends. Works while the Vulnerability scans module is off. 400 unknown_device, out_of_scope (outside the ranges, excluded, or the box), scope_not_confirmed, not_scannable (the device's safety rules refuse it); 409 module_off (sensor-active off), engine_off (active discovery off), already_running (a run a person started), busy (discovery is running nmap now), too_soon (a sweep less than 10 minutes ago; retry_after in seconds); 503 scanner_unavailable (nmap is not available)

targets.description: Leave out: sweep the whole LAN scope now, then identify the devices waiting for their scan ("Scan the LAN now"). Given: the devices to check now ("Check this device now", "Scan selected"), each an IPv4 address of a device or a device id. Every target must be a device inside the confirmed scope, outside the exclusions, and one its safety rules let a person check (a fragile device gets its gentle scan; "never scan" is refused)

post.summary: Add one LAN range to the scope where the person is ("+ New range" in a dialog, #842), without sending the whole block: read, append and save in one transaction, so it never overwrites another edit. The dialog lists the current ranges and whether they are confirmed with the confirmation tick, and sends both back (shown_ranges, shown_confirmed_at): the tick confirms those ranges and the new one only. 400 as PUT /scanning/safety for a range: no_prefix, bad_cidr, public_range, overlap_range, too_many_ranges (16), scope_too_large, and scope_not_confirmed when confirm is not true; 409 scope_changed (with error.safety, the current block) when the stored ranges are not shown_ranges or the stored confirmation is not shown_confirmed_at. A range the confirmed scope already covers is 200 with the block unchanged (no audit row). Audited as the PUT (inventory.settings, naming the range, and saying when the add confirmed a scope that was not confirmed) and publishes inventory.settings.changed. Returns the whole safety block with its new version, and adjusted when the range was normalized

progress.description: How far the current device is (#830): its phase, how far into it, an estimate of its end. Set while the run is running or stopping in this process; null otherwise

found.description: What the identification recorded, in words: "Operating system: …", "Type: …", "Software: …". The OS line keeps the OS only when it is the one the device page shows now; otherwise it reads "Operating system: scan guess not used now"

reason.description: null: software with a version was recorded and compared with the KEV list. Otherwise why nothing was: host_down (no answer), no_open_ports (all closed), filtered (scan incomplete: the device answered but no port it was asked about did; the device or a firewall dropped or slowed the probes; never shown as a fact that it filters), no_version (services gave no product or version), os_unconfirmed (only an OS guess: shown, never matched until a person adds the OS with its version), os_no_patch_level (the device named its Windows release and build in its NTLM answer, not its monthly update level: shown, never matched until a person adds it with its full version), os_low_confidence (OS guess under 85%), scope_not_confirmed, box (the box or a decoy), regular_scan_never, gentle_only (fragile: gentle scan only), timed_out (scan incomplete: nmap gave up on the host), busy (discovery was running nmap), unavailable (nmap not available or Active discovery off), declared_by_hand, scanning_off, not_approved, out_of_scope, no_ip, not_scanned

note.description: The box's sentence for the reason, shown as is

identification.description: One row per device of a Scan now run: what nmap identified first, or exactly why nothing was. Empty for scheduled scans and KEV rescans, and while the run is going

get.summary: Scannable targets and why others are not (unapproved device, out of scope, external IP the box has not seen for 30 days)

id.description: device id (a-nas02) or ext:<target id> for a verified external target

device_kind.description: Device type in the inventory; null for external targets

fragile.description: Fragile, or not yet classified (kind unknown): only scanned when picked by hand, at a quarter of the speed

pick_only.description: Fragile, unclassified or added by hand: scanned only when a person ticks it in Scan now. The page never ticks it for you: not by default, not with Select all, not from a link

reason.description: null when the target can be scanned by picking it. no_ip: the device has no IP address in the inventory. regular_scan_never: a person set "never scan" on the device. not_supported: external targets are not scanned by this version yet

box.description: The Vedette box itself: pick_only, so it is scanned only when a person ticks it; sweeps, schedules, KEV rescans and Select all never include it

mac.description: For the picker search; null when unknown and for external targets

vendor.description: For the picker search; null when unknown and for external targets

approved.description: Approved in the inventory (picker filter); false for external targets

last_seen.description: When the inventory last saw the device (picker filter); null for external targets

get.summary: One schedule with its next three start times, what it waits for, why its last due time was skipped and what its owner allows. Before anyone saves it: its owner's default (saved false). 404 not_found for a key no owner has, or a subject that does not exist

owner_key.description: What the schedule starts: scan.vuln, inventory.sweep, exposure.target:<id>, reports.def:<id>, feeds.source:<id>, ...

module.description: The module that owns it: a due time is skipped while it is off

saved.description: false: nobody saved it yet; enabled and rule are its default

paused_until.description: Due times before it are skipped: the next one counts from it

freq.description: interval: every every_minutes (with at_time, a whole number of days: every N days at that time); daily at at_time; weekly on weekdays at at_time; monthly on month_day at at_time; once at once_at

anyOf.description: HH:MM, 00:00 to 23:59, in the rule's zone

at_time.description: daily, weekly, monthly; interval only when every_minutes is whole days. A time the clocks skip when summer time starts comes due when they jump; a time they show twice comes due once

items.description: 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday

month_day.description: monthly only: 1 to 31, a month without that day runs on its last day; 0 = the last day

tz.description: "org" (the organization's time zone, Settings › General, the default) or an IANA zone such as Europe/Berlin

window.description: global: it starts only inside the box's scan window (Settings › Scanning › Safety), and a due time outside it waits for it to open; none: at any time; custom: only inside its own days and hours (window_days, window_from, window_to), and a due time outside them moves to their next opening

items.description: 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday

anyOf.description: HH:MM, 00:00 to 23:59, in the rule's zone

window_from.description: custom window only: when it opens

anyOf.description: HH:MM, 00:00 to 23:59, in the rule's zone

window_to.description: custom window only: when it closes; earlier than window_from = it crosses midnight and belongs to the day it opens on; equal = the whole day

rule.description: When a schedule comes due. The fields its frequency does not use are null (the box clears them when it saves)

zone.description: The IANA zone the rule is read in (the organization's for tz "org")

next_due_at.description: null while off or when it never comes due again (a once rule that ran)

upcoming.description: The next three start times: a due time in the past starts now, and one outside the scan window when it opens

waiting_for.description: Due, and held: what it waits for ("The scan window to open")

last_run_id.description: The run it last started (also by Run once now): open it at /runs/<id>

last_skip_reason.description: Why the last due time did not start anything ("The run it started at 20 Nov 2026, 23:00 had not ended.", "Its module is off."); null once a due time starts

updated_by.description: Who last changed it (an email, or system for a default); null while not saved

windows.description: The window modes its owner allows
